# Opt-In Vision Assist

Vision Assist gives an agentic browser run a tightly limited visual fallback when the page's text representation is incomplete or contradicts what the page is doing. It is off by default: until the user stores an explicit grant, Yantra does not register a screenshot tool or tell the model that one exists.

## What It Does

When Vision Assist is available, the agent may request `browser_screenshot` after text evidence has proved insufficient. The tool captures either the current viewport or one current Yantra element reference such as `e12`. Yantra briefly overlays its own `eNN` reference labels, takes a PNG through Chrome, removes the overlay, and sends one image block to the configured model.

The tool is registered only when all of these conditions hold:

- the effective `context.screenshots` preference is an approved boolean `true`;
- the command has browser tools and an active browser;
- the selected model explicitly declares image-input support;
- the invocation does not use `--no-screenshots`; and
- the execution is model-backed rather than a zero-LLM scheduled, daemon, or nested-workflow context.

If any registration condition is false or uncertain, the tool is absent from the model's catalog. Vision is never required for deterministic replay or for Yantra's browser interaction layer.

Every screenshot is subject to dedicated, fail-closed limits: at most 3 capture reservations per run, PNG only, no more than 1600 by 1200 pixels, and no more than 5 MiB of encoded PNG bytes per capture. A resolved website secret also latches the current top-level document against capture. Ordinary clicks, DOM changes, dialogs, subframe navigations, and same-document route changes do not clear that latch; capture becomes eligible only after a new top-level document loads or the browser is torn down.

Accepted captures are stored under the run directory as `screenshots/<sequence>-<sha256-prefix>.png`. `tool-calls.jsonl` and generated report projections contain capture metadata only: relative path, SHA-256, MIME type, dimensions, and byte count. They do not embed pixels. The raw provider session log under `agent/` contains the inline image sent to the model and is therefore a capture-bearing, sensitive local artifact. `yantra audit` calls this out and lists each image the model saw with its originating tool call and consumed capture budget.

## How to Use It

Grant screenshot access with the preference command:

```bash
yantra prefs set context.screenshots true
```

Before saving the grant, Yantra prints a warning that screenshots are raw, unmasked pixels the sanitizer cannot inspect. The warning names visible logged-in content, names, balances, message bodies, provider transmission, and local retention in both the run directory and raw provider session log. With Ollama, the destination says the image goes to the configured local model runtime rather than a remote provider; the rest of the warning remains. Under `--json`, the warning is emitted as a structured record before the successful set record.

Once granted, start a normal browser-capable agent run. Capture remains agent-requested fallback evidence; Yantra does not automatically attach screenshots after failures.

```bash
yantra do 'complete the requested browser task'
```

Suppress screenshots for one invocation without changing the stored grant:

```bash
yantra do 'complete the requested browser task' --no-screenshots
```

The same downward-only option is accepted by `ask` and `research`; it cannot enable Vision Assist on a command that has no browser capability. There is deliberately no `--screenshots` opt-in flag.

Revoke the grant by setting it to false or forgetting the preference:

```bash
yantra prefs set context.screenshots false
yantra prefs --forget context.screenshots
```

Revocation prevents future capture but does not delete images from earlier run directories. Inspect a completed run's capture trail with:

```bash
yantra audit <run-id>
yantra audit <run-id> --json
```

## Inputs and Outputs

The stored user input is the boolean preference `context.screenshots`. Only an approved value exactly equal to `true` grants access; absent, false, malformed, or unapproved values deny it. `--no-screenshots` can only suppress the saved grant for the current `do`, `ask`, or `research` invocation.

`browser_screenshot` accepts one optional `ref` matching Yantra's `eNN` element-reference format. With no reference, it captures the bounded viewport. With a reference, it captures that current element or returns `STALE_ELEMENT_REF` if the reference cannot be resolved.

A successful tool result gives the model bounded text metadata plus one PNG image. The persisted audit metadata for each capture is:

| Field             | Meaning                                |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `path`            | Run-relative path under `screenshots/` |
| `sha256`          | Digest used to verify the stored bytes |
| `mime_type`       | Always `image/png`                     |
| `width`, `height` | Captured dimensions in pixels          |
| `bytes`           | Encoded PNG size                       |

Capture can fail with `SCREENSHOT_SENSITIVE_SCREEN` while a secret-bearing document is latched, `STALE_ELEMENT_REF` for a no-longer-current element, `SCREENSHOT_UNAVAILABLE` when the page or capture cannot produce a complete valid artifact, or a capture-specific `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` result when count, dimensions, pixels, bytes, or MIME checks fail. Validation mismatches fail closed and the image is not forwarded.

## Configuration and Permissions

`context.screenshots` is part of the effective preference view merged from `~/.config/yantra/profile.yaml` and the machine preference store. The profile schema defaults it to `false`; `yantra init` also leaves it false. Values written by `yantra prefs set` are explicit user values and are approved by definition, while machine-learned, unapproved values cannot grant screenshot access.

The selected model must advertise image input in the model registry. A missing model, an unknown capability, or malformed registry data denies Vision Assist rather than guessing.

Screenshot directories and files use owner-only permissions (`0700` and `0600`) where the operating system supports those modes. This local restriction does not make the pixels sanitized: anyone who can read the run directory can inspect them, and the configured model provider receives the image during the run.

## Limitations

- Screenshot pixels bypass text sanitization by their nature. The grant warning, model-provider boundary, and local retention requirements apply even if a capture looks harmless.
- Vision Assist is a fallback, not a default observation path, an automatic recovery attachment, or a requirement for any supported interaction.
- The set-of-marks overlay labels only elements already known by Yantra and includes no page-derived text beyond those references and simple geometry.
- A secret-screen latch deliberately favors false denials: uncertainty about the top-level document epoch keeps capture disabled.
- Revoking the preference does not erase old screenshots or raw provider session logs. Remove old run directories using the same retention practices as other sensitive Yantra artifacts.
- Owner-only filesystem modes are best-effort on Windows and do not protect against other privileged local software.
